content.title: Secretary Hegseth recites fake bible quote from 'Pulp Fiction' during Pentagon prayer service
content.text: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth seemingly channeled his inner cinephile Wednesday, reciting a famous fictionalized Bible quote from "Pulp Fiction" during a Pentagon prayer service.While honoring the rescue mission of the downed airmen earlier this month in Iran, Hegseth asked the audience at the Pentagon's monthly Christian service to join him in prayer.He explained that the prayer he was to recite was the same one the service members said before carrying out the rescue mission. Hegseth said it was called "CSAR 25:17." CSAR stands for "combat search and rescue."“They call it CSAR 25:17, which I think is meant to reflect Ezekiel 25:17, so the prayer is CSAR 25:17, and it reads, and pray with me, please," Hegseth said. "'The path of the downed aviator is beset on all sides by the iniquities of the selfish and the tyranny of evil men. Blessed is he who, in the name of camaraderie and duty, shepherd the lost through the valley of darkness, for he is truly his brother’s keeper and the finder of lost children. And I will strike down upon thee with great vengeance and furious anger those who attempt to capture and destroy my brother. And you will know My call sign is Sandy-1 when I lay my vengeance upon thee. Amen.'"Watch the prayer in the video player above. Hegseth did not mention "Pulp Fiction" — or any other Quentin Tarantino movies — during the service. But viewers online quickly noted the striking similarities between Hegseth's prayer and the iconic monologue delivered by Samuel L. Jackson's character Jules Winnfield. A Public Witness, a religion and politics blog, was the first to report the apparent homage in Hegseth’s remarks.The line in the movie reads: "The path of the righteous man is beset on all sides by the inequities of the selfish and the tyranny of evil men. Blessed is he who, in the name of charity and good will, shepherds the weak through the valley of darkness, for he is truly his brother’s keeper and the finder of lost children, and I will strike down upon thee with great vengeance and furious anger those who attempt to poison and destroy my brothers. And you will know my name is the law when I lay my vengeance upon thee.”Jackson's character attributes the passage to Ezekiel 25:17. However, it is a fictionalized version of the actual passage. In the King James Bible, Ezekiel 25:17 reads: “And I will execute great vengeance upon them with furious rebukes; and they shall know that I am the Lord, when I shall lay my vengeance upon them.” According to Variety, Tarantino adapted the fake verse in “Pulp Fiction” from the 1973 Japanese martial arts film “Bodyguard Kiba,” retaining the false Ezekiel attribution and replacing “Chiba the Bodyguard” with “the Lord.” On Thursday, the Pentagon acknowledged the similarities between Hegseth's prayer and the movie's monologue.“Secretary Hegseth on Wednesday shared a custom prayer, referenced as the CSAR prayer, used by the brave warfighters of Sandy-1 who led the daylight rescue mission of Dude 44 Alpha out of Iran, which was obviously inspired by dialogue in Pulp Fiction," Sean Parnell, chief Pentagon spokesman, said on social media. "However, both the CSAR prayer and the dialogue in Pulp Fiction were reflections of the verse Ezekiel 25:17, as Secretary Hegseth clearly said in his remarks at the prayer service. Anyone saying the Secretary misquoted Ezekiel 25:17 is peddling fake news and ignorant of reality."Hegseth started the monthly Christian prayer services at the Pentagon in May 2025. Hegseth belongs to the Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches, a conservative network co-founded by the self-described Christian nationalist Doug Wilson.
